title: Raman spectroscopic study of microcrystalline silica
raman_evidence: Table 1 (printed p.271 = PDF p.3): Raman-active phonon frequencies of alpha quartz with mode symmetry, cm-1: 128 E(LO+TO), 206 A1, 265 E(LO+TO), 355 A1, 394 E(TO), 401 E(LO), 450 E(TO), 464 A1, 511 E(LO), 696 E(LO+TO), 796 E(TO), 808 E(LO), 1069 E(TO), 1085 A1, 1162 E(LO+TO), 1230 E(LO) (values of Hemley 1987, ambient); same table lists 19 moganite bands (129-1177); Fig. 2 spectra of moganite and pure-quartz chalcedony (Hope, Arizona) with laser plasma/air lines marked by asterisks
sample_description: Micro-Raman of microcrystalline silica (Gran Canaria moganite, Californian chalcedony, pure quartz chalcedony from Hope, Arizona); quartz column of Table 1 is single-crystal alpha quartz at ambient conditions, quoted from Hemley (1987)
notes: No DOI (Am. Mineral. 79, 269-273; authors K. J. Kingma and R. J. Hemley). Free PDF from the Mineralogical Society of America archive; the OCR text layer is poor (author names and table order garbled), so read Table 1 from a page render. Footnote of Table 1: 1-2 cm-1 differences between the table values (Hemley 1987) and peak positions in Figs. 1-2 come from small temperature differences. Moganite column is not needed for the quartz card.
